study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The introduction states the goals of using normative modelling to parameterize cortical thickness atypicality in ASD, compare it against traditional case–control analyses, identify prevalence of age-atypical CT, and relate individualized deviation scores to behavioural symptoms. These statements meet both criteria about research questions and the purpose of applying normative modelling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: “We examined how cortical thickness (CT) in ASD can be parameterized as an individualized metric of atypicality relative to typically-developing (TD) age-related norms… we applied normative modelling resulting in individualized whole-brain maps of age-related CT atypicality in ASD and isolating a small subgroup with highly age-atypical CT… we employ normative modelling… to isolate specific subsets of patients… Finally, we explore age-atypical CT-behaviour associations and assess whether such dimensional analyses… identify similar or different regions than typical case-control analyses.”

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort comprised TD participants from the ABIDE I/II datasets, with analyses using male-only TD data, citing the original dataset. They report matching, exclusion of failed segmentations, and removal of poor-quality scans using an Euler-index threshold, giving the final sample size. However, detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria for TD subjects and comprehensive image quality standards beyond the Euler cutoff are not fully described.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group (TD)… After matching case and control groups and excluding scans of poorer quality… we were left with a sample size N = 870 per group.”; “We excluded all subjects with a Euler score of 300 or higher in either hemisphere… after thresholding… the sample consisted of 870 individuals with autism and 870 neurotypical individual, matched on Age, Euler and IQ.”

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is explicitly modelled through age-binned normative curves, analyses are sex-stratified, and multi-site effects are handled with scanner site as a random effect. Additional confounds such as head motion and Euler index are included in models, demonstrating consideration of key covariates.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: “We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS)… computed median for each one-year age-bin… This was done separately for each sex.”; “We used a linear mixed effects model with scanner site as a random effect… included… age, in-scanner head motion and Euler index as covariates.”

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study specifies that normative data come from the openly available ABIDE I and II datasets and cites the source, satisfying the requirement to describe the data source of the reference cohort.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “We… utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II; 15)… Informed consent was given at each site included in the ABIDE studies.”

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The imaging data are from the existing ABIDE datasets rather than primary collection in this study, so acquisition protocol reporting is not applicable per the guideline.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described using FreeSurfer v5.3.0 recon-all with key steps (intensity normalization, skull stripping, WM segmentation, surface reconstruction) and QC procedures (Euler index computation, exclusion of failed subjects, thresholding high Euler scores).
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: “Cortical surface reconstruction was performed… with FreeSurfer… v5.3.0… recon-all involved intensity normalization, registration to Talairach space, skull stripping, WM segmentation, tessellation… CT… defined as the shortest distance between… WM boundary and the pial surface… We chose to not conduct manual segmentations and excluded failed subjects… To assess the quality of Freesurfer reconstructions we computed the Euler index.”; “We excluded all subjects with a Euler score of 300 or higher… after thresholding… the sample consisted of 870… matched on Age, Euler and IQ.”

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study reports hyperparameter optimization for LOESS bandwidth and evaluates reliability via 1000 bootstrap resamples of the normative sample, but it does not describe a partitioned validation strategy (e.g., hold-out or k-fold) where models are tested on unseen data.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “The local width or smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5–100% of the full age range using Brent’s method.”; “We bootstrapped the normative sample (1000 bootstraps… ) and computed 1000 bootstrapped w-scores… The median number of brain regions per subject with a significant p-value was 1… indicating that the w-score provides a robust measure of atypicality.”

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: All normative modelling is conducted on ABIDE I/II data with no application to an independent external healthy dataset, and no external validation set is described.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: “We… utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II).”

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The normative modelling approach is detailed as LOESS regression with bandwidth optimization, computation of age-binned normative means/SDs, and derivation of w-scores, with implementation details (Brent’s method via R optim).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: “We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS)… the local width… was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization… using Brent’s method… implemented in the R optim function… For each age bin and every brain region we computed a normative mean and standard deviation… The w-score for an individual thus reflects how far away their CT is from TD norms in units of standard deviation.”

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is probed through consistency checks (centile comparison and bootstrap reliability of w-scores) but no standard predictive performance metrics (e.g., explained variance or prediction error on held-out data) are reported.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: “We… assessed consistency of our output using centiles scoring and consistency of the normative model using extensive bootstrapping and sensitivity analyses, both showed high outcome consistency.”; “We bootstrapped the normative sample (1000 bootstraps… )… The median number of brain regions per subject with a significant p-value was 1… indicating that the w-score provides a robust measure of atypicality.”

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning (train/validation/test) of the normative cohort is reported; the modelling uses the full TD sample, so partition-specific characteristics are not applicable.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software versions and pipelines are specified (FreeSurfer v5.3.0, R packages), and the study provides open access to data and code with repository links, fulfilling reproducibility criteria.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: “Cortical surface reconstruction was performed… with FreeSurfer… v5.3.0… recon-all…”; “All data is openly available on GitHub… Original unprocessed neuroimaging data is openly available through the ABIDE consortium…”; “All code is openly available on GitHub… Cohen’s d were computed using: https://github.com/mvlombardo/utils/blob/master/cohens_d.R and the centiles cross-validation code can be found in https://github.com/deep-introspection/PyNM.”

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort (ASD) is drawn from ABIDE I/II with age matching and exclusions for poor image quality (failed reconstructions and Euler >300), and the final sample size is given. However, detailed diagnostic criteria and full inclusion/exclusion standards for patients are not described within this paper.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “We utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II)… After matching case and control groups and excluding scans of poorer quality… we were left with a sample size N = 870 per group.”; “We excluded all subjects with a Euler score of 300 or higher… after thresholding… the sample consisted of 870 individuals with autism and 870 neurotypical individual.”

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses incorporate clinical and phenotypic covariates beyond demographics, including ADOS, SRS, SCQ, AQ, IQ, and age in brain–behaviour correlations, and models include motion and Euler indices as confounds.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: “We also conducted some exploratory analysis… computed Spearman correlations… between… ADOS, SRS, SCQ, AQ, FIQ and Age.”; “linear mixed effects model including site, sex, age, in-scanner head motion and Euler index as covariates.”

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The ASD clinical cohort is explicitly sourced from the ABIDE I/II datasets, an existing database, satisfying the requirement to describe the data source.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: “We utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II; 15)….”

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: The paper provides sample sizes and demographic/clinical characteristics, including age statistics by sex and diagnosis (Table 2) and clinical measures such as IQ, ADOS, and SRS with means, SDs, and Ns (Table 3).
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table 2 lists age characteristics by diagnosis and sex (e.g., Autism Male N=754… TD Male N=660). Table 3 lists clinical measures (IQ, ADOS, SRS) with means, SD, and N for autism and controls by sex.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessment tools used in analyses are specified, including ADOS and SRS scores reported in Table 3 and used in symptom correlations with w-scores.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: Table 3 includes ADOS and SRS measures with means and sample sizes; “computed Spearman correlations… for… ADOS, SRS, SCQ, AQ, FIQ and Age.”

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The manuscript defines w-scores as deviations from age-specific TD norms, explains that ±2 SD thresholds identify atypical individuals, and discusses their prevalence and behavioural associations, covering meaning, thresholds, and clinical relevance of deviation scores.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: “The w-score for an individual thus reflects how far away their CT is from TD norms in units of standard deviation.”; “We then describe the prevalence of ASD cases that show meaningful age-related deviance in CT (i.e. >2 standard deviations from age-related norms)….”; “To isolate subsets of individuals with significant age-related CT deviance, we used a cut-off score of 2 standard deviations (i.e. w >= 2 or w<=2)….”
